ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a triangle, with vertices roughly at the upper left, lower left, and right side. The upper-left angle is labeled x°, and the lower-left angle is labeled 48°. The side from the upper left to the right side is labeled 53, and the side from the lower left to the right side is labeled 68. Reasoning: Side 53 is opposite the 48° angle, and side 68 is opposite the x° angle. Use the sine rule: sin(x)/68 = sin(48°)/53. Therefore sin(x) = 68sin(48°)/53 ≈ 0.9534, x = arcsin(0.9534) ≈ 72.45°. In the figure, x is an acute angle, so take the acute-angle solution, and rounding to the nearest integer gives 72°.

method.method_draft: From the image, identify a single triangle with vertices at the upper-left, lower-left, and right. The side from upper-left to right is labeled 53, the side from lower-left to right is labeled 68, the lower-left interior angle is 48°, and the upper-left interior angle is x°. From the text, note that x is an angle measure and must be rounded to the nearest degree. Use the Law of Sines: the side of length 53 is opposite the 48° angle, and the side of length 68 is opposite x, so set sin(x)/68 = sin(48°)/53. Solve x = arcsin(68 sin(48°)/53). Because the diagram shows x as the acute upper-left angle, choose the acute arcsine value rather than the supplementary SSA alternative, then round to the nearest degree to get 72.
